items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: I imagine bringing Bonk to New York probably exposed him to all kinds of... remarks around New York

ctx.x: Defensive kind of thing, in other words. Yeah, yeah. Just... It's always been interesting to me, uh... the musicians and the... uh... people who follow jazz, are constantly forced to put up this kind of defensive thing, I think, if you get involved in the thing.

Yeah, well, particularly with this kind of music, uh... you're open to a lot of ridicule, and, uh... there are always the, uh... the know-nothings who, uh... who give constant mockery at every effort to, uh... help the music along. I mean, I imagine bringing Bonk to New York probably exposed him to all kinds of... remarks around New York, so... Well, there's a lot of nudniks, you know,
who caught up with these 19th century ideas of progress. I think they ought to get up to date. Yeah. You know what I mean? Yeah. And they really don't look at things
